rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Fatiha is Meccan and has seven verses; Muslims recite it at least seventeen times daily, more with voluntary prayers, and may repeat it without limit.
rows.anchor: الفاتحة مكية وآياتها سبع

rows.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
rows.claim: The Prophet says prayer is invalid without reciting the Opening of the Book; the report is in both Sahih collections.
rows.anchor: لا صلاة لمن لم يقرأ بفاتحة الكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The short surah gathers core Islamic creed, worldview, feelings, and guidance, explaining its repetition in every rakʿa and why prayer without it is invalid.
rows.anchor: ما يشير إلى طرف من حكمة اختيارها للتكرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Against disagreement over the basmala's status, Quṭb prefers counting it as a verse of al-Fatiha, making the surah seven verses.
rows.anchor: فإن الأرجح أنها آية من سورة الفاتحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed view takes the seven oft-repeated verses in 15:87 to be al-Fatiha, seven verses repeated in prayer.
rows.anchor: وهناك قول بأن المقصود بقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning in God's name is the etiquette revealed to the Prophet at the first revelation and accords with God as First, Last, Manifest, and Hidden.
rows.anchor: والبدء باسم الله هو الأدب الذي أوحى الله لنبيه [ ص ] في أول ما نزل من القرآن باتفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is the true existent from whom every existence and beginning derives, every beginning, movement, and direction should start in His name.
rows.anchor: فهو - سبحانه - الموجود الحق الذي يستمد منه كل موجود وجوده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rahman and Rahim together encompass every meaning and condition of mercy; God alone bears both, and alone may be called Rahman, though a servant may be called Rahim.
rows.anchor: فمن الجائز أن يوصف عبد من عباده بأنه رحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb leaves aside which mercy-name has broader scope and stresses that together they cover mercy in all its meanings, conditions, and domains.
rows.anchor: إنما نخلص منه إلى استغراق هاتين الصفتين مجتمعتين لكل معاني الرحمة وحالاتها ومجالاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning in God's name expresses the first major Islamic worldview principle, God's oneness and proper reverence; comprehensive mercy expresses the second and defines the bond between God and servants.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان البدء باسم الله وما ينطوي عليه من توحيد الله وأدب معه يمثل الكلية الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After invoking the Merciful God, the worshipper turns to praise Him and name His unrestricted lordship over all worlds.
rows.anchor: وعقب البدء باسم الله الرحمن الرحيم يجيء التوجه إلى الله بالحمد ووصفه بالربوبية المطلقة للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praising God wells up in a believer's heart at His mention: existence itself and ceaseless blessings call forth praise.
rows.anchor: والحمد لله هو الشعور الذي يفيض به قلب المؤمن بمجرد ذكره لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise begins and ends the Islamic worldview; the Qur'an says God alone is deity and that praise belongs to Him in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم كان الحمد لله ابتداء

rows.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet described a servant's expansive praise, which two angels could not record; God ordered them to write it as spoken and promised reward when the servant meets Him.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله [ ص ] حدثهم أن عبدا من عباد الله قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase Lord of the worlds states a core creed: God's complete lordship extends across all creation.
rows.anchor: فالربوبية المطلقة الشاملة هي إحدى كليات العقيدة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, rabb can mean master or the one who manages, reforms, and nurtures; God continuously tends every creature rather than leaving the universe unattended.
rows.anchor: ويطلق في اللغة على السيد وعلى المتصرف للإصلاح والتربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Recognizing God's unrestricted lordship separates clear monotheism from beliefs that combine one creator with multiple powers governing life.
rows.anchor: والربوبية المطلقة هي مفرق الطريق بين وضوح التوحيد الكامل الشامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some polytheists claimed they worshipped lesser patrons only to bring them nearer to God, while some People of the Book treated their rabbis and monks as lords.
rows.anchor: اتخذوا أحبارهم ورهبانهم أربابا من دون الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making God Lord of all worlds points away from a chaotic crowd of competing lords toward one sovereign, bringing order, certainty, and confidence in His constant care.
rows.anchor: فإطلاق الربوبية في هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quṭb contrasts Islam's continuing divine care with Aristotle's alleged view that God creates the cosmos and then ignores it as beneath His attention.
rows.anchor: لا كما كان أرقى تصور فلسفي لأرسطو مثلا يقول بأن الله أوجد هذا الكون ثم لم يعد يهتم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human conscience could not settle questions of the cosmos, the self, and life before it reached clear certainty about God, His attributes, and His relation to creation.
rows.anchor: ولم يكن مستطاعا أن يستقر الضمير البشري على قرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islam therefore concentrated on freeing creed from every ambiguity through pure, comprehensive monotheism and an unambiguous account of God's absolute lordship.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم كان التوحيد الكامل الخالص المجرد الشامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Comparing Islam's simple, coherent account of God with the inherited tangle of beliefs reveals this creed as mercy for heart and mind.
rows.anchor: عندئذ تبدو العقيدة الإسلامية رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mercy-names form a separate verse to underscore mercy as the defining feature of comprehensive lordship and the enduring relationship between Creator and creatures.
rows.anchor: هذه الصفة التي تستغرق كل معاني الرحمة وحالاتها ومجالاتها تتكرر هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's bond with servants is mercy and care, which elicit praise, reassurance, and affection, unlike vindictive or capricious gods in Greek myths and the Babel story in Genesis 11.
rows.anchor: إن الرب الإله في الإسلام لا يطارد عباده مطاردة الخصوم والأعداء كآلهة الأولمب في نزواتها وثوراتها كما تصورها أساطير الإغريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik conveys the highest sovereignty and control, and the Day of Religion is the day of recompense in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: والملك أقصى درجات الاستيلاء والسيطرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people acknowledged God as deity and original creator but still denied the Day of Recompense; the Qur'an notes that they would identify God as creator when asked.
rows.anchor: وكثيرا ما اعتقد الناس بألوهية الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an also recounts deniers' amazement at a human warner and their objection that resurrection after becoming dust is far-fetched.
rows.anchor: أئذا متنا وكنا ترابا ؟  ذلك رجع بعيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Belief in the afterlife directs hearts beyond earthly needs and anxieties, enabling people to rise above them and work for God with confidence in His chosen reward.
rows.anchor: والاعتقاد بيوم الدين كلية من كليات العقيدة الإسلامية ذات قيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith in final recompense divides human freedom from enslavement to desires and earthly values, and separates full humanity from distorted forms.
rows.anchor: بين الخضوع لتصورات الأرض وقيمها وموازينها والتعلق بالقيم الربانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A God-centered human life requires assurance that earthly reward is not final and that another life warrants struggle and sacrifice for truth and good.
rows.anchor: وما تستقيم الحياة البشرية على منهج الله الرفيع ما لم تتحقق هذه الكلية في تصور البشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who believe in the afterlife differ from its deniers in feeling, character, conduct, and work, and will differ in earthly action and ultimate recompense.
rows.anchor: وما يستوي المؤمنون بالآخرة والمنكرون لها في شعور ولا خلق ولا سلوك ولا عمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding principles entail that worship and reliance belong to God alone.
rows.anchor: وهذه هي الكلية الاعتقادية التي تنشأ عن الكليات السابقة في السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive worship liberates people from subjection to other people, systems, social arrangements, superstition, and delusion.
rows.anchor: وهذه الكلية تعلن ميلاد التحرر البشري الكامل الشامل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should support and cooperate for good with human forces that believe in God and follow His way, and resist and change those disconnected from God and His way.
rows.anchor: وهذه يجب أن يؤازرها ، ويتعاون معها على الخير والحق والصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A misguided human power may look immense but loses its true strength when severed from God, while even a small force connected to Him retains power.
rows.anchor: تفقد الغذاء الدائم الذي يحفظ لها طاقتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A small faithful group can overcome a larger one through connection to the first source of strength, as the Qur'an says in 2:249.
rows.anchor: غلبتها باتصالها بمصدر القوة الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims should approach natural powers through understanding and friendship, since human and natural forces share God's will and cooperate under it.
rows.anchor: وأما القوى الطبيعية فموقف المسلم منها هو موقف التعرف والصداقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made natural forces helpful allies; people gain their aid by observation, knowledge, and cooperation, while harm often follows ignorance of their laws.
rows.anchor: إن عقيدة المسلم توحي إليه أن الله ربه قد خلق هذه القوى كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Western phrase “conquer nature” reflects a worldview severed from God; Muslims see nature's forces as created under one law for cooperative ends and thank God for their service.
rows.anchor: ولهذا التعبير دلالته الظاهرة على نظرة الجاهلية المقطوعة الصلة بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God, not humanity, subjects natural forces to human use; the Qur'an says He subjected all that is on earth for people.
rows.anchor: فالله هو الذي يسخرها له

rows.speaker: رسول الله [ ص ]
rows.claim: Looking toward Mount Uhud, the Prophet said that the mountain loves the Muslims and they love it, exemplifying intimacy with nature.
rows.anchor: وما أروع قول الرسول [ ص ] وهو ينظر إلى جبل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God both to show the connected, straight road and to keep the worshippers upright on it; knowing and following it are gifts of His guidance and care.
rows.anchor: وفقنا إلى معرفة الطريق المستقيم الواصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance to the straight path is the believer's greatest and first request because it certainly secures happiness in both worlds and aligns human nature with God's law and creation.
rows.anchor: وهذا الأمر هو أعظم وأول ما يطلب المؤمن من ربه العون فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The straight path is that of people granted God's favor, not those who know truth and turn away in anger or those who never find guidance to truth.
rows.anchor: فهو طريق الذين قسم لهم نعمته

rows.speaker: رسول الله
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports in Sahih Muslim that God calls al-Fatiha a prayer divided between Himself and His servant: praise, mercy, and glorification are the Lord's; worship and aid are shared; guidance and the servant's request belong to the servant, who receives what he asks.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة عن رسول الله [ ص ] :  "  يقول الله تعالى : قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Aʿla is Meccan and has nineteen verses; the Prophet loved it, recited it at Eid and Friday prayers with al-Ghashiya, sometimes on the same day.
rows.anchor: سورة الأعلى مكية وآياتها تسع عشرة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports that the Prophet loved this surah; Muslim reports that he recited it with al-Ghashiya at Eid and on Friday, sometimes reciting both on one day.
rows.anchor: أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] كان يحب هذه السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah turns the entire cosmos into a sanctuary reverberating with praise and offers the Prophet good news of divine preservation and ease in his mission and affairs.
rows.anchor: وحق لرسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] أن يحب هذه السورة وهي تحيل له الكون كله معبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its foundations are God's oneness as creator, divine revelation, and afterlife recompense, rooted in earlier scriptures; it also portrays the easy nature of the message, messenger, and community.
rows.anchor: وهي تتضمن الثابت من قواعد التصور الإيماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening's relaxed, extended rhythm releases echoes of glorification and displays the Creator's work throughout existence.
rows.anchor: ليطلق في الجو ابتداء أصداء التسبيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasbih is exaltation and declaring God transcendent, with inward awareness and lived experience of His beautiful attributes, rather than merely repeating “Subhan Allah.”
rows.anchor: والتسبيح هو التمجيد والتنزيه واستحضار معاني الصفات الحسنى لله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabb means nurturer and caretaker, a tender shade fitting the surah; al-Aʿla directs the spirit toward endless horizons and coheres with exaltation.
rows.anchor: والصفة الأولى القريبة في هذا النص هي صفة الرب . وصفة الأعلى . . والرب : المربي والراعي

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet responded directly to the command by reciting “Glory to my Lord Most High,” embodying immediate closeness and obedience.
rows.anchor: وقد كان رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] يقرأ هذا الأمر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When this verse descended, the Prophet instructed worshippers to include its glorification in prostration; when 56:74 descended, he assigned that verse to bowing.
rows.anchor: وحينما نزلت هذه الآية قال :  "  اجعلوها في سجودكم  "

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permission to praise and connect with God is itself a divine favor, given in a form people can grasp and glimpse of His attributes.
rows.anchor: فإذن الله لعباده بأن يحمدوه ويسبحوه إحدى نعمه عليهم وأفضاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates each thing, perfects its making, and brings it to the completeness appropriate to it.
rows.anchor: الذي خلق كل شيء فسواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns every creature its function and end, guides it to its purpose, and provides and guides it toward what sustains it throughout its life.
rows.anchor: والذي قدر لكل مخلوق وظيفته وغايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After surveying vast existence, the surah completes its great glorification with an evocative image from plant life.
rows.anchor: وبعد عرض هذا المدى المتطاول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-marʿa means all vegetation, broader than pasture for livestock; God apportions provisions on earth for every creature that walks, hides underground, or flies.
rows.anchor: فهو هنا أشمل مما نعهده من مرعى أنعامنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vegetation begins green then withers into dark, almost black debris; it can feed creatures in either state, each suited to some purpose in life by God's measure.
rows.anchor: والمرعى يخرج في أول أمره خضرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plant's withering quietly suggests that every growth is harvested and every living thing ends, linking worldly life to the enduring afterlife.
rows.anchor: والإشارة إلى حياة النبات هنا توحي من طرف خفي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The broad cosmic frame connects the surah's subsequent truths to existence, and similarly frames many surahs in this section in harmony with their mood and rhythm.
rows.anchor: وبهذا المطلع الذي يكشف عن هذا المدى المتطاول من صفحة الوجود الكبيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception “unless God wills” preserves the unrestricted divine will even after the promise of preservation, keeping hearts continually attached to that will.
rows.anchor: فهو الاحتراس الذي يقرر طلاقة المشيئة الإلهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of what is public and hidden explains the preceding preservation and exception: His decisions follow wisdom informed by full knowledge of every aspect.
rows.anchor: وكأن هذا تعليل لما مر في هذا المقطع من الإقرار والحفظ والاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We ease you toward ease” promises ease to the Prophet and his community and defines the religion, its mission, and its place in existence.
rows.anchor: بشرى لشخص الرسول [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] وبشرى لأمته من ورائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's easing links the Prophet, religion, and cosmos: existence itself emerges easily, moves easily, and proceeds easily toward its goal.
rows.anchor: الوجود الخارج من يد القدرة في يسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person God eases moves gently with the ordered universe and events; ease shapes his speech, steps, work, thought, and dealings with himself and others.
rows.anchor: اليسر في يده . واليسر في لسانه

rows.speaker: الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Aisha reports that when given two choices, the Prophet selected the easier; when at home, he was the gentlest of people, smiling and laughing.
rows.anchor: ما خير بين أمرين إلا اختار أيسرهما كما روت عنه عائشة - رضي الله عنها -

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim describes the Prophet's clothing as varied and unforced, chosen according to what was available and fitting; sometimes he let a turban's tail hang and sometimes not.
rows.anchor: شمس الدين أبي عبد الله محمد بن قيم الجوزية

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim says the Prophet ate available pleasant food without demanding what was absent, never criticized food, and left disliked food without declaring it forbidden; he ate a lizard while companions watched.
rows.anchor: لا يرد موجودا ولا يتكلف مفقودا

rows.speaker: ابن قيم الجوزية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Qayyim recounts the Prophet sleeping on varied surfaces, from a bed, mat, or ground to a couch or black cloth.
rows.anchor: كان ينام على فراشه تارة وعلى النطع تارة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet teaches that religion is easy and that whoever makes it onerous will be overcome by it; al-Bukhari is cited.
rows.anchor: إن هذا الدين يسر ، ولن يشاد الدين أحد إلا غلبه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns against imposing strictness, saying that earlier people imposed it on themselves and it was imposed on them; Abu Dawud is cited.
rows.anchor: لا تشددوا على أنفسكم فيشدد عليكم فإن قوما شددوا على أنفسهم

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares an overburdened traveler to one who neither crosses the land nor preserves his mount; al-Bukhari is cited.
rows.anchor: إن المنبت لا أرضا قطع ولا ظهرا أبقى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet instructs people to make matters easy rather than difficult; both Sahih collections are cited.
rows.anchor: يسروا ولا تعسروا  "  [ أخرجه الشيخان ]

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet asks God's mercy for a person who is gracious when selling, buying, and collecting payment; al-Bukhari is cited.
rows.anchor: رحم الله رجلا سمحا إذا باع وإذا اشترى وإذا اقتضى

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet describes a believer as gentle and easygoing; al-Bayhaqi is cited.
rows.anchor: المؤمن هين لين  "  [ أخرجه البيهقي ]

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that a believer forms relationships and is welcomed by others; al-Daraqutni is cited.
rows.anchor: المؤمن يألف ويؤلف  "  [ أخرجه الدارقطني ]

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says God most hates a contentious, quarrelsome person; both Sahih collections are cited.
rows.anchor: إن أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn al-Musayyib recounts from his father that the Prophet changed his name from Hazn (hardness) to Sahl (ease); his father refused, and Saʿid said hardness remained among them; al-Bukhari is cited.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب عن أبيه - رضي الله عنه - أنه جاء للنبي

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that the Prophet changed the name ʿAsiya to Jamila; Muslim is cited.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما - أن رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] غير اسم عاصية وسماها جميلة

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says that greeting one's brother with a cheerful face is an act of kindness; al-Tirmidhi is cited.
rows.anchor: إن من المعروف أن تلقى أخاك بوجه طلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's fine sensibility noticed harshness even in names and faces and turned toward gentleness, reflecting his God-given nature and ease-oriented formation.
rows.anchor: فهو الحس المرهف الذي يلمح الوعورة والشدة حتى في الأسماء والملامح فينفر منها

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: When a Bedouin insulted him after receiving a gift, the Prophet stopped his companions from retaliating, privately gave the man more, and arranged public reconciliation so their resentment would pass.
rows.anchor: جاءه أعرابي يوما يطلب منه شيئا فأعطاه

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet explains that he handled the man like an owner calmly retrieving a frightened runaway camel, and warns that killing the Bedouin would have sent him to Hell.
rows.anchor: إن مثلي ومثل هذا الأعرابي كمثل رجل كانت له ناقة شردت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentle, simple, effective handling of alienated people exemplifies how the Prophet's life and mission fulfilled God's promise to ease him.
rows.anchor: فهكذا كان أخذه [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] للنفوس الشاردة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's ease made the great trust of the message a beloved, joyful practice rather than a crushing burden.
rows.anchor: حيث تتحول الرسالة بهذا التيسير من عبء مثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an calls the Prophet a mercy to the worlds; 7:157 describes him as known in Torah and Gospel, commanding good, forbidding wrong, permitting wholesome things, prohibiting foul things, and lifting burdens and shackles.
rows.anchor: وما أرسلناك إلا رحمة للعالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The message itself is easy: 54:17 makes the Qur'an easy to remember; 22:78 and 5:6 reject hardship; 2:286 limits duty to capacity; even commanded duties must be done as far as one can.
rows.anchor: ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر فهل من مدكر

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet says to do what one can of a command, avoid what is prohibited, and recognizes necessity as an exception to prohibitions; the passage gives no collection or grading.
rows.anchor: إذا أمرتكم بأمر فأتوا منه ما استطعتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The creed is simple and obligations flow from it coherently; people fulfill them within their capacity, and necessities may exempt them from prohibited things.
rows.anchor: والتكاليف بعد ذلك كلها تنبثق من هذه العقيدة في تناسق مطلق لا عوج فيه ولا انحراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The easy-going Prophet and easy message produced a balanced, merciful community whose nature aligns with the easy nature of the universe.
rows.anchor: فهي الأمة الوسط ، وهي الأمة المرحومة الحاملة للرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cosmos moves without collision or disorder: celestial bodies, living beings, and events all proceed toward their ends in measured harmony, like instruments joining one melody.
rows.anchor: ملايين الملايين من الأجرام تسبح في فضاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The universe, message, Prophet, and Muslim community are in complete accord as creations of the one God.
rows.anchor: إنه التوافق المطلق بين طبيعة الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is equipped by God's recitation, preservation, and easing so he may remind; he should remind wherever there is an opening, access to hearts, and a means to communicate.
rows.anchor: فذكر حيثما وجدت فرصة للتذكير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminder always benefits someone, somewhere, in every generation and land, however corrupt people become or hardened their hearts grow.
rows.anchor: ولن تعدم من ينتفع بها كثيرا كان أو قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The order of the verses reveals the mission's weight: God equips the Prophet with recitation, preservation, and ease so he can bear the great task of reminder.
rows.anchor: وحين نتأمل هذا الترتيب في الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet fulfills his duty by reminding; people then diverge in response and outcome, and God deals with them according to how they receive the reminder.
rows.anchor: فإذا نهض [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] بهذا العبء فقد أدى ما عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The God-fearing person benefits from reminder because a living heart senses awe of God's anger and punishment, and knows the Creator will account for and justly repay good and evil.
rows.anchor: ذلك الذي يستشعر قلبه التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wretched person avoids reminder and refuses to hear or benefit from it; al-ashqa names the absolute endpoint of wretchedness.
rows.anchor: يتجنب الذكرى ، فلا يسمع لها ولا يفيد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this life the utterly wretched has a dead, dull soul that cannot sense existence's truths or respond to its signs and lives anxiously grasping at trivial worldly concerns.
rows.anchor: الأشقى في الدنيا بروحه الخاوية الميتة الكثيفة الصفيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His afterlife is made wretched by punishment without known end, described in the following verses.
rows.anchor: والأشقى في الآخرة بعذابها الذي لا يعرف له مدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The great Fire is Hell, great in intensity, duration, and vastness, where the wretched person remains for a long time.
rows.anchor: والنار الكبرى هي نار جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The damned person cannot die and find relief or live in safety and comfort; he endures eternal torment and longs for death.
rows.anchor: الذي يتطلع صاحبه إلى الموت كما يتطلع إلى الأمنية الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success and salvation lie on the other side of wretchedness, through purification and remembrance; tazakki means cleansing oneself of every stain and defilement.
rows.anchor: والتزكي : التطهر من كل رجس ودنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God's name means inwardly recalling His majesty; “then he prayed” may mean humble devotion and submission.
rows.anchor: فاستحضر في قلبه جلاله : ( فصلى ) . . إما بمعنى خشع وقنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “then he prayed” may mean canonical ritual prayer; either sense can arise from inward remembrance, awareness of God's majesty, and reverence.
rows.anchor: فكلاهما يمكن أن ينشأ من التذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One who purifies, remembers, and prays certainly prospers: in this life through a living connection and the sweetness of remembrance, and in the next through escape from Hell and attaining bliss and approval.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي تطهر وذكر وصلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preferring worldly life is the root of affliction and neglect: remembrance calls people to account for and prefer the afterlife, while they want and choose this world.
rows.anchor: إن إيثار الحياة الدنيا هو أساس كل بلوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dunya is so named because it is both nearer and lower, base and transient.
rows.anchor: إلى جانب أنها الدانية : العاجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is superior in kind and longer in duration; preferring worldly life over it is foolish misjudgment no clear-sighted person would make.
rows.anchor: خير في نوعها ، وأبقى في أمدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's foundational creed is ancient, rooted in the first scriptures of Abraham and Moses.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي ورد في هذه السورة وهو يتضمن أصول العقيدة الكبرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Truth and creed are one because their source and the will behind sending messengers are one; details vary with changing needs and eras but return to the same root.
rows.anchor: إنه حق واحد ، يرجع إلى أصل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The core truths of this surah were present in Abraham's and Moses' scriptures; the creed's shared source is the Lord who creates, perfects, apportions, and guides.
rows.anchor: إن هذا لفي الصحف الأولى صحف إبراهيم وموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghashiya is Meccan and has twenty-six verses; its quiet, deep cadences prompt reflection, hope, fear, and preparation for the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: سورة الغاشية مكية وآياتها ست وعشرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah moves through two vast fields, the hereafter and the visible world with its signs, then recalls reckoning, God's dominion, and inevitable return to Him.
rows.anchor: في مجالين هائلين : مجال الآخرة وعالمها الواسع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question conveys grandeur and a previously declared reminder; al-Ghashiya names the overwhelming calamity that covers people with terrors, alongside other suggestive names for Resurrection in this section.
rows.anchor: وبهذا الإستفهام الموحي بالعظمة الدال على التقدير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ghashiya means the catastrophe that envelops people and overwhelms them with its terrors; names such as al-Tamma, al-Sakhkha, and al-Qariʿa fit this section's atmosphere.
rows.anchor: أي الداهية التي تغشى الناس وتغمرهم بأهوالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet felt the direct address “Has the account come to you?” as personally directed to him whenever he heard the surah.
rows.anchor: كان رسول الله [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] يحس وقع توجيهه إلى شخصه

rows.speaker: عمر بن ميمون
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from Umar ibn Maymun that the Prophet passed a woman reciting al-Ghashiya, stopped to listen, and answered, “Yes, it has come to me”; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن عمر بن ميمون ، قال : مر النبي [ صلى الله عليه وسلم ] على امرأة تقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address also applies to everyone who hears the Qur'an; repeated warning and good news stir vigilance, awe, hope, and expectation so consciences stay awake.
rows.anchor: عام لكل من يسمع هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah presents torment before bliss because punishment better fits the overwhelming mood and shade of al-Ghashiya.
rows.anchor: إنه يعجل بمشهد العذاب قبل مشهد النعيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that Day faces are humbled, abased, exhausted, and distressed; their work brought neither praise nor a good outcome, only loss that deepens their anguish and weariness.
rows.anchor: يومئذ وجوه خاشعة ذليلة متعبة مرهقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These people labored for other than God, themselves, children, worldly life, and desires; they received misery here without provision and torment there, meeting the end as defeated failures.
rows.anchor: عملت لغير الله ، ونصبت في غير سبيله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Along with humiliation and exhaustion, they face a scorching fire and taste its pain.
rows.anchor: ومع هذا الذل والرهق العذاب والألم : ( تصلى نارا حامية )وتذوقها وتعانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are given water from a spring at extreme heat.
rows.anchor: ( تسقى من عين آنية ) . . حارة بالغة الحرارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says ḍariʿ is a tree of fire in Hell, based on reports that the zaqqum tree grows at the root of the Inferno.
rows.anchor: استنادا إلى ما ورد عن شجرة الزقوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view identifies ḍariʿ as low-growing thorny shibriq: camels graze it green, but once cut it becomes ḍariʿ, which even camels cannot taste because it is poisonous.
rows.anchor: ترعاه الإبل وهو أخضر ، ويسمى
